title: 2.2.22 Challenges: Stretch Problems
description: Stretch problems. Every challenge is required to continue. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: designed: stretch problems informed by book Problem Set 2.2.1 (FizzBuzz-style) and Key Terms review

steps.title: FizzBuzz 1 to 20
steps.instructions: Loop through the integers 1 to 20. For each number: if it is divisible by both 3 and 5 (`i % 3 === 0` is true when i divides evenly by 3: the remainder is 0), log 'FizzBuzz'. If divisible by only 3, log 'Fizz'. If divisible by only 5, log 'Buzz'. Otherwise log the number itself.

steps.title: Count vowels
steps.instructions: Given a string, count how many characters are vowels (a, e, i, o, u: upper or lower case). Log the total count.

steps.title: Sum even numbers
steps.instructions: Loop through every integer from 1 to 20. Add up only the even numbers (use the % operator to test) and log the total.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "2.2.22 Challenges: Stretch Problems". The task they were given: Loop through the integers 1 to 20. For each number: if it is divisible by both 3 and 5 (`i % 3 === 0` is true when i divides evenly by 3: the remainder is 0), log 'FizzBuzz'. If divisible by only 3, log 'Fizz'. If divisible by only 5, log 'Buzz'. Otherwise log the number itself. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
